outcome_detail: State-court Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act suit in Eaton County Circuit Court and a September 2025 federal suit in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Michigan remain active; coverage as recent as April 2026 describes ongoing litigation, including perjury allegations against a lieutenant colonel over an affidavit filed in the state case. The plaintiff prevailed twice in arbitration over her terminations and received back pay in May 2025 described as a 'MAKE WHOLE SETTLEMENT,' but the civil rights lawsuits themselves are unresolved.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges reported against the officials accused in the lawsuits. In 2026 the plaintiff filed a criminal complaint alleging perjury by Lt. Col. Aimee Brimacombe over an affidavit in the civil case; no charges have been reported. The plaintiff herself faced criminal charges stemming from an October 2020 incident, which her suit characterizes as retaliatory.
description: A former Michigan State Police trooper sued the agency in Eaton County Circuit Court under Michigan's Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act, alleging systemic gender discrimination, sexual harassment, and retaliation within what she described as a 'Big Boys' Club' culture. According to the complaint, she faced repeated investigations, criminal charges, and two terminations after she reported harassment and assisted another agency's officer in filing a criminal complaint against an MSP trooper who allegedly secretly recorded consensual sex. Arbitrators twice ruled in her favor on her terminations. In September 2025 she filed a related federal lawsuit in the Western District of Michigan naming Col. James F. Grady and Lt. Col. Aimee Brimacombe, alleging they made false sworn statements in the state case and had firsthand knowledge of the retaliation. The suits, which arose from allegations aired in an extensive WLNS 6 News investigative series, remain pending.
